articles.title: Quay crane investment programme completed at port of Southampton
articles.summary: Associated British Ports has welcomed the arrival of two further quay cranes at DP World Southampton, completing a GBP 60 million investment programme that represents Europe’s largest quay crane investment and further strengthening Southampton’s position as a leading UK gateway for global trade. The delivery of the...
articles.body: Associated British Ports has welcomed the arrival of two further quay cranes at DP World Southampton, completing a GBP 60 million investment programme that represents Europe’s largest quay crane investment and further strengthening Southampton’s position as a leading UK gateway for global trade. The delivery of the final two cranes completes a set of four, which together enhance Southampton’s ability to accommodate the world’s largest container ships and support continued growth in international trade. The completion marks the latest in a series of significant milestones for the Port of Southampton in 2026, a year that has also seen successful calls by some of the world’s largest cruise, automotive and container vessels. Alastair Welch, ABP Regional Director for Southampton, congratulated DP World on the crane deliveries and described the completion as the latest in a line of landmark achievements for the port in 2026, reaffirming ABP’s ambition for Southampton’s role in supporting jobs, trade and economic growth. The container terminal, operated by DP World, handles approximately two million containers annually, connecting UK businesses with global markets, and is owned and managed by ABP as part of its continued investment in infrastructure supporting long-term port success, supply chain resilience and regional economic development.
takeaways: The delivery of the final two cranes completes a set of four, which together enhance Southampton’s ability to accommodate the world’s largest container ships and support continued growth in international trade.

articles.title: Port of Dakar advances digitalization plans with IMO support
articles.summary: Senegal is moving forward with plans to digitalize port procedures at the Port of Dakar, following a needs assessment conducted with support from the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The assessment, carried out from 5 to 9 October, examined the port’s existing processes and institutional arrangements to...
articles.body: Senegal is moving forward with plans to digitalize port procedures at the Port of Dakar, following a needs assessment conducted with support from the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The assessment, carried out from 5 to 9 October, examined the port’s existing processes and institutional arrangements to identify the requirements for introducing a Maritime Single Window (MSW). The proposed system would allow ships and public authorities to exchange information through a single digital platform, simplifying administrative procedures for vessel arrivals, stays and departures. IMO assesses digital requirements at Port of Dakar During the mission, IMO consultants worked with Senegal’s National Agency of Maritime Affairs (ANAM), the port administration and several government agencies. These included customs, port health authorities, border police and immigration services. Representatives from shipping lines, shipping agents and terminal operators also participated in the consultations. The assessment focused on identifying operational and institutional requirements for developing the Maritime Single Window. An MSW is designed to reduce duplicate paperwork, improve coordination between authorities and simplify port clearance procedures. Since 1 January 2024, IMO Member States have been required to establish, maintain and use Maritime Single Window systems in ports. Roadmap to guide port digitalization Following the assessment, a comprehensive report will outline a roadmap for developing the system at the Port of Dakar. The report will identify the stakeholders involved, define their responsibilities and assess the operational requirements for implementation. It will also provide recommendations for deploying the Maritime Single Window and developing supporting digita

articles.body: Hambantota International Port has surpassed one million TEUs in cumulative container throughput since the commissioning of new quay cranes in 2025, marking a significant milestone in the rapid growth of its container operations. The port handled 428,036 TEUs in 2025 and 574,196 TEUs year-to-date in 2026, bringing combined volume to 1,002,232 TEUs. MSC, HIP’s principal container customer, has contributed significantly to the growth trajectory. In April 2026, the MSC Marie Leslie set a new single-vessel handling record of 7,968 container moves, equivalent to 13,260 TEUs, during a single call. HIP subsequently achieved its highest-ever monthly throughput of 80,325 TEUs in June, reflecting operational preparedness and available capacity during a period of uncertainty affecting major global trade routes. To support sustained growth toward a long-term target of two million TEUs annual capacity, HIP is undertaking a US$ 108 million expansion programme encompassing six new quay cranes and 16 rubber-tyred gantry cranes, expected to be commissioned by the end of February 2027. Once operational, the new equipment will strengthen ship-to-shore and yard-handling capacity, support utilisation of an additional 1,300 metres of berth space and take total container quay length to nearly two kilometres. The container yard will be expanded by 30% to accommodate rising throughput, and reefer capacity will also be increased. articles.body: GEODIS has obtained a new certification in Poland, enabling the logistics company to provide specialized transport services for the defence sector, including the handling of strategically important goods and dual-use products. The company secured the Internal Compliance Programmes (ICP) certificate, which confirms that its internal procedures meet specific security and regulatory compliance requirements. The certification expands GEODIS’ capabilities in Poland, allowing it to serve customers whose shipments are subject to strict national and European Union regulations. These include companies transporting goods, technologies and services classified as strategically important, as well as products with both civilian and military applications. Certification strengthens specialized transport services The certificate was issued by CCJ, an accredited certification body operating within the Military University of Technology in Poland. To obtain the certification, GEODIS reviewed and updated its internal procedures, conducted audits, trained employees and established responsibilities for its internal control system. The system will remain subject to ongoing supervision and periodic assessments. “This is another step in the development of specialist services of GEODIS in Poland,” said Marc Vollet, EVP of European Road Network at GEODIS. The certification also supports the company’s ability to work with customers requiring additional safeguards for supply chain security, information access and regulatory compliance. New opportunities in defence logistics With the certification in place, GEODIS can pursue additional opportunities in Poland’s specialized logistics market, particularly among businesses operating in regulated sectors. articles.title: Construction of wind turbines has begun at Port of Zeebrugge
articles.summary: Preparatory groundworks have commenced this month for the construction of eight new wind turbines in the port of Zeebrugge, with a total capacity of 42.6 MW, in a joint investment by ENGIE, Port of Antwerp-Bruges and Portfineco, a vehicle jointly owned by Zefier and Port of Antwerp-Bruges. ENGIE will manage the...
articles.body: Preparatory groundworks have commenced this month for the construction of eight new wind turbines in the port of Zeebrugge, with a total capacity of 42.6 MW, in a joint investment by ENGIE, Port of Antwerp-Bruges and Portfineco, a vehicle jointly owned by Zefier and Port of Antwerp-Bruges. ENGIE will manage the operational management of the turbines through the joint venture company Seagull I. Three of the eight turbines will be located on the premises of the Wallenius Wilhelmsen RoRo terminal, with the remaining five sited on the premises of International Car Operators, where ENGIE, ICO and Portfineco already commissioned an 11-turbine wind farm of 44 MW capacity in 2020. Tower masts, nacelles and blades are scheduled for installation in the second half of 2027, with the turbines expected to begin generating approximately 115 gigawatt-hours of renewable electricity annually from the start of 2028, equivalent to the average consumption of approximately 33,000 Belgian households. Vincent Verbeke, CEO of ENGIE Belgium, described the project as part of the company’s focus on large-scale renewable development in port and industrial areas, strengthening Zeebrugge’s role as an energy hub for the region. Dirk De fauw, Vice-Chairman of Port of Antwerp-Bruges and Mayor of Bruges, noted that the project brings the port well on its way to reaching half a gigawatt of installed wind capacity across its platforms by 2030. Henk Kindt, Chairman of Zefier, highlighted Portfineco’s participation as reflecting the cooperative’s commitment to renewable energy benefiting its 160 shareholder municipalities.
takeaways: ENGIE will manage the operational management of the turbines through the joint venture company Seagull I.

articles.title: TT Club and UK P&I Club secure member approval for merger
articles.summary: TT Club and UK P&I Club have secured approval from their members for a proposed merger that will bring together two major insurance organisations serving the global maritime, container and logistics industries. The decision was confirmed following separate Special General Meetings held on 7 and 8 October 2026. The...
articles.body: TT Club and UK P&I Club have secured approval from their members for a proposed merger that will bring together two major insurance organisations serving the global maritime, container and logistics industries. The decision was confirmed following separate Special General Meetings held on 7 and 8 October 2026. The merger is scheduled to take effect on 20 February 2027, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals. The combined organisation will operate under a new parent company, United Transport Mutual Limited (UTM), with annual premium income of approximately US$750 million and free reserves of around US$888 million. Combined group to cover shipping, ports and logistics The merger will bring together the UK P&I Club’s marine insurance operations and TT Club’s activities across container transport, ports, terminals and logistics. According to the organisations, UK P&I Club insures more than 250 million tonnes of owned and chartered shipping tonnage, while TT Club provides insurance coverage for 80% of the world’s container fleet. TT Club also has an insurable interest in more than 70 of the world’s 100 largest ports, giving the proposed group a substantial presence across maritime transport and cargo handling operations. The two organisations expect the combination to strengthen their financial resources and expand access to specialist expertise in underwriting, claims management and loss prevention. The merger is also expected to generate an overall 5% improvement in the combined ratio, a key measure of underwriting performance. Despite the integration, both clubs will retain their existing names, brands and market positions. Their members will continue to be served by their respective underwriting, claims and service teams. articles.title: Port of Los Angeles sets monthly cargo record
articles.summary: The Port of Los Angeles handled 1,042,652 TEUs in September 2026, the busiest month in the port’s 118-year history, surpassing the previous monthly record set in July 2025 by more than 20,000 units. The record month capped the busiest quarter in port history, with nearly 3 million TEUs handled from July through...
articles.body: The Port of Los Angeles handled 1,042,652 TEUs in September 2026, the busiest month in the port’s 118-year history, surpassing the previous monthly record set in July 2025 by more than 20,000 units. The record month capped the busiest quarter in port history, with nearly 3 million TEUs handled from July through September, while the four-month stretch from June through September produced nearly 4 million TEUs, also the strongest such period on record. Loaded imports reached 545,696 TEUs in September, up 19% year-on-year, while loaded exports totalled 125,751 TEUs, up 10%. Empty containers reached approximately 371,206 TEUs, the highest monthly total in port history. Through the first nine months of 2026, the port has handled nearly 8.1 million TEUs, more than 3% ahead of the same period last year. Executive Director Gene Seroka attributed the record performance to resilient consumer demand, inventory replenishment by importers, and cargo allocation shifting toward Los Angeles as shippers navigate challenges along Suez Canal and Panama Canal routes. He also noted that tariffs are lower than levels seen earlier in the year, giving importers greater cost certainty. Harvard Business School Professor Willy Shih, joining the monthly media briefing, described a broader shift in corporate supply chain strategy from pure cost optimisation toward flexibility in sourcing, manufacturing and cargo routing amid continued global trade uncertainty. Mayor Karen Bass credited the port’s waterfront workforce, the ILWU and Executive Director Seroka for the historic result, describing the port as an extraordinary economic engine supporting good-paying union jobs and maintaining Los Angeles’s status as a global trade and commerce competitor.
takeaways: The Port of Los Angeles handled 1,042,652 TEUs in September 2026, the busiest month in the port’s 118-year history, surpassing the previous monthly record set in July 2025 by more than 20,000 units.
Loaded imports reached 545,696 TEUs in September, up 19% year-on-year, while loaded exports totalled 125,751 TEUs, up 10%.
Empty containers reached approximately 371,206 TEUs, the highest monthly total in port history.

articles.title: Container freight rates weaken as Asia-Europe decline continues
articles.summary: Global container freight rates remained under pressure in the latest weekly readings, with several major benchmarks declining around China’s Golden Week holiday period. Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) fell 2%, while the China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI) and Ningbo Containerized Freight Index (NCFI) also...
articles.body: Global container freight rates remained under pressure in the latest weekly readings, with several major benchmarks declining around China’s Golden Week holiday period. Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) fell 2%, while the China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI) and Ningbo Containerized Freight Index (NCFI) also moved lower. The Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) was broadly stable, and the Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) recorded almost no change. At trade-lane level, the latest readings showed mixed conditions across the Transpacific, while Asia-Europe continued its downward trend. Chinese freight indexes show mixed performance The SCFI edged up 0.05% to 3,664.11 points, compared with 3,662.30 in the previous reading. The broader CCFI declined 0.6% to 1,912.38 points from 1,923.93. The NCFI also moved lower, falling approximately 1.5% to 2,431.78 points from 2,468.61 in the previous reading. The latest figures show that the Chinese benchmarks remain mixed, although two of the three recorded declines. NYFI highlights diverging Transpacific trends The latest NYSHEX Freight Index (NYFI) , published on 9 October, showed different movements across the two major Asia-US routes. Asia-US West Coast declined 1.98% to 7,407.75, reversing the 1.89% increase recorded in the previous reading. Asia-US East Coast moved in the opposite direction, rising 1.40% to 9,831.24 after remaining almost unchanged in the previous assessment. Asia-North Europe continued to weaken, falling another 3.24% to 3,356.23. The Transatlantic market also showed contrasting movements. Westbound rates edged down 0.52% to 2,709.05, while eastbound rates increased 8.23% to 1,282.09. articles.body: Maersk will increase its Import and Export Fuel Surcharge for US inland haulage from 1 November 2026. The Maersk US inland fuel surcharge will rise from US$140 to US$215 per container. Charge Current rate New rate Import/Export Fuel Surcharge US$140 per container US$215 per container Scope of the Maersk US inland fuel surcharge The revised surcharge will apply to shipments carried under a Maersk ocean bill of lading when the carrier arranges trucking to or from the customer’s door within the United States. It will apply to shipments with a Price Calculation Date on or after 1 November 2026. The charge will appear separately on the bill of lading under the IFS or EFS code. Maersk attributed the adjustment to rising US diesel prices. The carrier said the 13-week average diesel price increased by more than US$0.10 per gallon, adding pressure to linehaul, drayage, depot and first-mile transportation costs.
